newsitem.title: USA: GM Delphi '96 non-NAO sales rise from '95.
newsitem.headline: GM Delphi '96 non-NAO sales rise from '95.

text.p: Delphi Automotive Systems, the auto parts unit of General Motors Corp, said Thursday that 36.1 percent of its 1996 sales were to customers outside of GM's North American Operations (NAO) unit.

For 1995, the figure was 33.3 percent. Delphi has a goal of receiving 50 percent of its total sales from non-NAO customers by 2002. Although the figure excludes sales to GM's North American operations, it does include sales to GM's overseas operations.
Total worldwide sales for Delphi in 1996 were $27.8 billion about flat with 1995, which the company blamed on labor problems in the U.S. and Canada during the first and fourth quarters of 1996.
Delphi's Asia-Pacific region sales were $1.5 billion; European (including the Middle East, Africa and Russia) sales totaled $4.5 billion; South American sales were $800 million.
"We continue to operate strongly in the black," J.T. Battenberg III, president of Delphi, said in a statement.

Delphi completed 20 new ventures, either joint ventures, acquisitions or all new plants, in 1996, bringing its total ventures worldwide to 46. The company introduced 55 new products and processes in 1996, completed the sale of four manufacturing plants in North America and announced the closure of two facilities in Europe.

"These are very tough decisions, but we have got to focus our entire organization on meeting the realities of the competitive challenges in this industry," Battenberg said. "We must continually measure ourselves against our competitors and find innovative solutions to the competitive challenges we face."
